15.text: Polio is caused by Poliovirus.
Polio is a viral disease.
Polio has humans as hosts.
Polio is transmitted by the fecal–oral route.
Polio can spread through contaminated food or water.
Polio affects the spinal cord and central nervous system.
Polio can cause paralysis.
COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2.
COVID-19 is a viral disease.
COVID-19 has humans as hosts.
COVID-19 spreads through respiratory transmission.
COVID-19 spreads through contact.
COVID-19 affects the respiratory system.
COVID-19 can cause multi-organ complications.
Rabies is caused by rabies lyssavirus.
Rabies is a viral zoonotic disease.
Rabies has dogs, cats, bats, foxes and other animals as hosts or sources.
Rabies is transmitted through bites or scratches.
Rabies transmission involves saliva.
Rabies affects the nervous system.
Rabies can cause hydrophobia.
Hepatitis-B is caused by HBV.
Hepatitis-B is a viral disease.
Hepatitis-B has humans as hosts.
Hepatitis-B spreads through blood and body fluids.
Hepatitis-B spreads through sexual transmission.
Hepatitis-B can spread from mother to child.
Hepatitis-B affects the liver.
Mumps is caused by mumps virus.
Mumps is a viral disease.
Mumps has humans as hosts.
Mumps spreads through saliva and nasal secretions.
Mumps spreads through contact.
Mumps affects the salivary or parotid glands.
Dengue is caused by dengue virus.
Dengue is a viral disease.
Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.
Dengue transmission occurs through mosquito bites.
Dengue can decrease platelet levels.
Chikungunya is caused by CHIKV.
Chikungunya is a viral disease.
Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus.
Chikungunya is transmitted through mosquito bites.
Chikungunya causes severe joint pain.
Zika is caused by Zika virus.
Zika is a viral disease.
Zika is associated with Aedes mosquitoes.
Zika can spread through mosquito transmission.
Zika can spread through blood transmission.
Zika can spread through sexual transmission.
Zika can cause fever.
Zika can cause rash.
Zika can cause joint pain.
Yellow fever is caused by yellow fever virus.
Yellow fever is a viral disease.
Yellow fever is transmitted by Aedes aegypti.
Yellow fever is transmitted through mosquito bites.
Yellow fever causes fever.
Yellow fever can cause haemorrhagic disease.
AIDS is caused by HIV.
AIDS is a viral retrovirus-related disease.
AIDS has humans as hosts.
AIDS spreads through blood transmission.
AIDS spreads through sexual transmission.
AIDS can spread from mother to child.
AIDS affects the immune system.
Ebola is caused by Ebola virus.
Ebola is a viral zoonotic disease.
Ebola has animals and non-human primates as sources or hosts.
Ebola can spread from animals to humans.
Ebola can spread through human-to-human transmission.
Ebola causes haemorrhagic disease.
Nipah is caused by Nipah virus.
Nipah is a viral zoonotic disease.
Nipah has animals as sources or hosts.
Pigs are discussed as a source of Nipah.
Nipah can spread through animal-to-human transmission.
Nipah can spread through human transmission.
Nipah causes severe viral disease.
Measles is caused by measles virus.
Measles is a viral disease.
Measles has humans as hosts.
Measles spreads through respiratory transmission.
Measles is highly contagious.
Japanese encephalitis is caused by JEV.
Japanese encephalitis is a viral disease.
Japanese encephalitis is associated with Culex mosquitoes.
Pigs and wild birds are reservoirs for Japanese encephalitis.
Japanese encephalitis is transmitted through mosquito bites.
Japanese encephalitis affects the brain.
Ranikhet or Newcastle disease is caused by a virus.
Ranikhet or Newcastle disease is a viral disease.
Ranikhet or Newcastle disease affects chickens.
Ranikhet or Newcastle disease is infectious in poultry.
Rinderpest is caused by Morbillivirus.
Rinderpest is a viral disease.
Rinderpest affects cattle and buffaloes.
Rinderpest is contagious among livestock.
Bird flu is caused by H5N1.
Bird flu is a viral disease.
Bird flu is associated with birds and poultry.
Bird flu can spread from birds to humans.
Bird flu can involve human transmission.
Bird flu affects the respiratory system.
Swine flu is caused by H1N1.
Swine flu is a viral disease.
Pigs are hosts for swine flu.
Swine flu affects the respiratory system.
Swine flu is associated with influenza.
Foot and mouth disease is caused by Aphthovirus.
Foot and mouth disease is a viral disease.
Foot and mouth disease affects cattle, goats, pigs and sheep.
Foot and mouth disease is infectious among cloven-hoofed animals.
Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae.
Cholera is a bacterial disease.
Cholera has humans as hosts.
Cholera spreads through contaminated food or water.
Cholera affects the small intestine.
Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis or Pasteurella pestis.
Plague is a bacterial disease.
Plague involves a rat–flea cycle.
Fleas act as vectors for plague.
Plague affects the lymph nodes.
Plague can cause buboes.
Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae or M. lepromatosis.
Leprosy is a bacterial disease.
Leprosy has humans as hosts.
Leprosy is infectious.
Leprosy affects the skin.
Leprosy affects peripheral nerves.
Pneumonia is mainly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and other organisms.
Pneumonia can have bacterial causes.
Pneumonia can have viral causes.
Pneumonia can have fungal causes.
Pneumonia has humans as hosts.
Pneumonia is infectious.
Pneumonia affects the lungs.
Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi.
Typhoid is a bacterial disease.
Typhoid has humans as hosts.
Typhoid spreads through contaminated food or water.
Typhoid affects the intestinal tract.
Diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
Diphtheria is a bacterial disease.
Diphtheria has humans as hosts.
Diphtheria spreads through respiratory transmission.
Diphtheria affects the throat and nose.
Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Gonorrhoea is a bacterial disease.
Gonorrhoea has humans as hosts.
Gonorrhoea spreads through sexual transmission.
Gonorrhoea affects the reproductive organs.
Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum.
Syphilis is a bacterial disease.
Syphilis has humans as hosts.
Syphilis spreads through sexual transmission.
Syphilis affects the genitals, rectum and mouth.
Pertussis is caused by Bordetella pertussis.
Pertussis is a bacterial disease.
Pertussis has humans as hosts.
Pertussis spreads through respiratory transmission.
Pertussis causes whooping cough.
Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani.
Tetanus is a bacterial disease.
Tetanus is associated with soil and other sources.
Tetanus can follow a contaminated wound.
Tetanus causes muscle spasms.
Tetanus can cause jaw involvement.
Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.
Tuberculosis has humans as hosts.
Tuberculosis spreads through respiratory transmission.
Tuberculosis affects the lungs.
Rheumatic fever is associated with Streptococcus pyogenes.
Rheumatic fever can follow an infection.
Rheumatic fever can affect the heart.
Rheumatic fever can affect the brain.
Rheumatic fever can affect the joints.
Rheumatic fever can affect the skin.
Botulism is caused by Clostridium botulinum toxin.
Botulism is a bacterial intoxication.
Botulism is associated with food, wounds and infants.
Botulism can involve food or wound transmission.
Botulism affects the nerves.
Botulism can cause paralysis.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium.
Malaria is a protozoan disease.
Malaria is associated with female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Malaria can spread through blood transfusion.
Malaria can spread through needles.
Malaria affects the liver and red blood cells.
Malaria can cause an enlarged spleen.
Kala-azar is caused by Leishmania.
Kala-azar is a protozoan disease.
Kala-azar is associated with sandflies.
Dogs are reservoirs for Kala-azar.
Kala-azar can spread through sandflies.
Kala-azar can spread through blood and needles.
Kala-azar affects the liver, spleen and bone marrow.
Sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma brucei.
Sleeping sickness is a protozoan disease.
Sleeping sickness is transmitted by tsetse flies.
Sleeping sickness is transmitted through bites.
Sleeping sickness affects the brain and central nervous system in later stages.
Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
Amoebiasis is a protozoan disease.
Amoebiasis has humans as hosts.
Amoebiasis spreads through contaminated food or water.
Amoebiasis affects the intestine.
Schistosomiasis is caused by Schistosoma.
Schistosomiasis is caused by a parasitic flatworm.
Snails are intermediate hosts for schistosomiasis.
Schistosomiasis is associated with unsafe water.
Schistosomiasis affects the urinary tract and intestine.
Fascioliasis is caused by Fasciola hepatica or Fasciola gigantica.
Fascioliasis is caused by a parasitic worm.
Ruminants are the main hosts for fascioliasis.
Fascioliasis can spread through raw water plants.
Fascioliasis affects the liver and bile ducts.
Neurocysticercosis is caused by Taenia solium eggs.
Neurocysticercosis is caused by a parasite.
Neurocysticercosis has humans as hosts.
Neurocysticercosis spreads through contaminated food or water.
Neurocysticercosis affects the brain and central nervous system.
Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti.
Filariasis is a nematode disease.
Filariasis is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes.
Filariasis is transmitted through mosquito bites.
Filariasis affects the lymph glands.
Filariasis can cause elephantiasis.
Ascariasis is caused by Ascaris lumbricoides.
Ascariasis is a nematode disease.
Ascariasis has humans as hosts.
Ascariasis spreads through ingestion of eggs.
Ascariasis affects the small intestine.
Athlete's foot is caused by Trichophyton, Epidermophyton and Microsporum.
Athlete's foot is a fungal disease.
Athlete's foot has humans as hosts.
Athlete's foot can spread through contaminated floors, towels or clothes.
Athlete's foot affects the skin of the foot.
Mucormycosis is caused by Mucormycetes.
Mucormycosis is a fungal disease.
Mucormycosis has the environment as a source.
Mucormycosis has no specified vector.
Mucormycosis can affect the nose, sinuses, eyes and brain.
Aspergillosis is caused by Aspergillus.
Aspergillosis is a fungal disease.
Aspergillosis is associated with humans, birds and animals.
Aspergillosis can be respiratory or systemic.
Ergotism is caused by Claviceps purpurea toxin.
Ergotism is a fungal intoxication.
Ergotism is associated with rye and cereals.
Ergotism can spread through ingestion.
Ergotism affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems.
Cancer involves abnormal cell growth.
Cancer is associated with oncogene mutations.
Cancer is non-contagious.
Cancer can affect any organ.
Cancer can involve metastasis.
Leukaemia involves abnormal white blood cell production.
Leukaemia is non-contagious.
Leukaemia affects the bone marrow and blood.
Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency.
Goitre is a deficiency disease.
Goitre affects the thyroid.
Beriberi is caused by vitamin B1 deficiency.
Beriberi is a deficiency disease.
Beriberi affects the heart and nervous system.
Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency.
Kwashiorkor is a deficiency disease.
Kwashiorkor affects growth and the liver.
Marasmus is caused by energy and protein deficiency.
Marasmus is a deficiency disease.
Marasmus causes severe wasting.
Night blindness is caused by vitamin A deficiency.
Night blindness is a deficiency disease.
Night blindness affects the eye.
Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency.
Rickets is a deficiency disease.
Rickets affects the bones.
Scurvy is caused by vitamin C deficiency.
Scurvy is a deficiency disease.
Scurvy affects connective tissue and gums.
Pellagra is caused by niacin or vitamin B3 deficiency.
Pellagra is a deficiency disease.
Pellagra affects the skin, gastrointestinal system and nervous system.

14.text: Aristotle classified animals.
Aristotle is associated with zoology.
Aristotle is known as the Father of Zoology.
Birbal Sahni studied plant fossils.
Birbal Sahni worked in palaeobotany.
Birbal Sahni contributed to Indian palaeobotany.
Linnaeus developed binomial nomenclature.
Linnaeus worked in taxonomy.
Linnaeus formalised modern classification.
Leeuwenhoek studied bacteria and microorganisms.
Leeuwenhoek worked in microbiology.
Leeuwenhoek made the first observation of bacteria.
Robert Hooke studied the cell.
Robert Hooke worked in cell biology.
Robert Hooke observed the cell.
Robert Hooke named the cell.
Robert Brown discovered the nucleus.
Robert Brown worked in cell biology.
Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory.
Schleiden and Schwann worked in cell biology.
The cell is the basic structural unit.
Virchow proposed the pre-existing-cell principle.
Virchow worked in cell biology.
New cells arise from existing cells.
Lamarck proposed Lamarckism.
Lamarck worked in evolution.
Lamarck proposed the inheritance of acquired characters.
Charles Darwin proposed natural selection.
Charles Darwin worked in evolution.
Charles Darwin explained evolution by natural selection.
Hugo de Vries proposed the Mutation Theory.
Hugo de Vries worked in evolution and genetics.
Hugo de Vries identified mutation as an evolutionary mechanism.
Oparin and Haldane proposed chemical evolution.
Oparin and Haldane worked on the origin of life.
Oparin and Haldane proposed an origin-of-life hypothesis.
Mendel formulated the laws of inheritance.
Mendel worked in genetics.
Mendel laid the foundation of modern genetics.
Barbara McClintock studied transposable elements.
Barbara McClintock worked in genetics.
Barbara McClintock discovered jumping genes.
Friedrich Miescher studied DNA and nuclein.
Friedrich Miescher worked in molecular biology.
Friedrich Miescher first identified DNA.
Friedrich Miescher first isolated DNA.
Watson, Crick, and Wilkins worked on the DNA double helix.
Watson, Crick, and Wilkins worked in molecular biology.
Watson, Crick, and Wilkins developed a structural model of DNA.
Arthur Kornberg studied DNA synthesis and DNA polymerase.
Arthur Kornberg worked in molecular biology.
Arthur Kornberg demonstrated DNA synthesis in vitro.
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley studied the genetic code.
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley worked in molecular biology.

Landsteiner studied ABO blood groups.
Landsteiner worked in hematology.
Landsteiner developed the modern blood-group system.
Landsteiner and Wiener studied the Rh factor.
Landsteiner and Wiener worked in immunohematology.
Landsteiner and Wiener identified the Rh factor.
Ronald Ross studied malaria transmission.
Ronald Ross worked in parasitology.
Ronald Ross established that Plasmodium occurs in mosquitoes.
Ronald Ross established mosquito transmission of malaria.
Banting, Macleod, and Best studied insulin.
Banting, Macleod, and Best worked in endocrinology.
Banting, Macleod, and Best discovered and isolated insulin.
Hans Krebs studied the Krebs cycle.
Hans Krebs worked in biochemistry.
Hans Krebs identified a cellular-respiration pathway.
Embden, Meyerhof, and Parnas studied glycolysis, also known as EMP.
Embden, Meyerhof, and Parnas worked in biochemistry.
Embden, Meyerhof, and Parnas described the glycolytic pathway.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin.
Alexander Fleming worked in microbiology and medicine.
Alexander Fleming made an antibiotic discovery.
Gerhard Domagk discovered Prontosil.
Gerhard Domagk worked in medicine.
Gerhard Domagk discovered an antibacterial drug.
Selman Waksman discovered streptomycin.
Selman Waksman worked in microbiology.
Selman Waksman made an antibiotic discovery.
Edward Jenner developed smallpox vaccination.
Edward Jenner worked in immunology.
Jonas Salk developed the polio vaccine.
Jonas Salk worked in virology.
Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine.
Albert Sabin developed the oral polio vaccine.
Albert Sabin worked in virology.
Albert Sabin developed oral polio vaccination.
Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting.
Alec Jeffreys worked in genetics and forensics.
Lalji Singh worked on Indian DNA fingerprinting.
Lalji Singh worked in molecular biology.
Lalji Singh established DNA-fingerprinting technology in India.
J. C. Bose studied plant growth.
J. C. Bose worked with the Crescograph.
J. C. Bose worked in plant physiology.
The Crescograph measures plant growth.
Karl von Frisch studied bee communication.
Karl von Frisch worked in animal behaviour.
Karl von Frisch identified circle dances and waggle dances.
Köhler and Milstein developed hybridoma technology.
Köhler and Milstein worked in biotechnology and immunology.
Köhler and Milstein developed monoclonal antibodies.
Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell were associated with Dolly cloning.
Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell worked in biotechnology.
Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell carried out somatic-cell cloning.
Gurdev Khush Singh worked on Super Rice.
Gurdev Khush Singh worked in plant genetics and agriculture.

Arvid Carlsson studied dopamine and Parkinson's disease.
Arvid Carlsson worked in neuropharmacology.

Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun studied microRNA.
Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun worked in molecular biology.

Brunkow, Ramsdell, and Sakaguchi studied regulatory T cells and FOXP3.

1.text: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was the first person to explain evolution to the public.
Lamarckism was the first broad theory of organic evolution.
The first fossils of Archaeopteryx were discovered at Solnhofen, Germany.
Louis Lartet discovered the first Cro-Magnon skull.
The first Denisovan individual was identified in 2010.
A.P. de Candolle was the first to use vascular tissues in plant classification.
A.P. de Candolle first coined the term taxonomy.
Triticale was the first man-made cereal crop.
Schleiden and Schwann proposed the first theory of cell structure, known as cell theory.
Prokaryotic cells were the first form of life.
Camillo Golgi was the first person to observe the Golgi body.
Barbara McClintock first identified transposable elements.
Friedrich Miescher first identified or isolated DNA.
DNA was first identified or isolated in 1869.
Gregor Mendel conducted the first hybridization experiments on pea.
Watson and Crick first outlined the structure of the DNA or gene molecule.
Watson and Crick first proposed the double-helix model of DNA.
Watson and Crick proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953.
DNA polymerase I was the first known DNA polymerase.
Arthur Kornberg is associated with DNA polymerase I.
Yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, was the first organism with a complete eukaryotic genome sequenced.
The complete eukaryotic genome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae was sequenced in 1996.
Karl Landsteiner made the first blood-group classification.
Karl Landsteiner made the first blood-group classification in 1900.
William Harvey first discovered blood circulation.
Dr Christian Barnard performed the world's first human heart transplant.
The world's first human heart transplant was performed in 1967.
South Africa was the country of the first human heart transplant.
Barney Clark was the first recipient of an artificial heart.
Barney Clark received an artificial heart in 1982.
IgM is the first antibody produced in a primary infection.
hCG is the first hormone released by the placenta.
hCG is also called chorionic gonadotropin.
The human embryo's heart first begins beating during the fourth to fifth week.
Oxaloacetic acid is the first organic compound formed in C4 photosynthesis.
Oxaloacetic acid is abbreviated as OAA.
Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, was the site of the first biodiesel plant in India.
Jonas Salk first successfully developed a polio vaccine.
The smallpox vaccine was the first vaccine in the world.
Edward Jenner was the first scientist or doctor to attempt vaccination.
Edward Jenner attempted vaccination in 1796.
Insulin was the first human hormone produced by recombinant-DNA technology.
Recombinant insulin, also called Humulin, was the first drug produced through recombinant-DNA technology.
Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell.
Dolly was a sheep.
Dolly was the first successfully cloned animal.
Dolly was the first living cloned genetically engineered organism.
Dolly was born on 5 July 1996.
Dolly was born in Scotland.
Samrupa was the world's first cloned buffalo.
Samrupa was cloned in 2009.
Ganga was India's first cloned cow.
Ganga was of the Gir breed.
Injaz was the world's first cloned camel.
The first transgenic glowing pigs were produced in Taiwan.
The first transgenic glowing pigs were produced in 2006.
The Flavr Savr tomato was the first commercially grown genetically engineered food.
Bollgard-I Bt cotton was India's first biotech crop technology approved for commercialisation.
Bollgard-I Bt cotton was approved for commercialisation in 2002.
The first crime solved using DNA fingerprinting was a murder investigation in England.
The first crime solved using DNA fingerprinting occurred in 1983.
Schizosaccharomyces pombe was the yeast cited for the first microbial semiconductor-diode fabrication.
Saheli was the world's first non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill.
Dubai, UAE, was the site of the world's first camel hospital.
Hyderabad was the site of India's first dinosaurium.
R. Ahmed Dental College in Kolkata was the first dental college in India.
R. Ahmed Dental College was established in 1920.
Jaya was the first dwarf rice variety developed in India.
Bhutan was the first country to ban the sale of tobacco and tobacco products.
Bhutan imposed the tobacco-sale ban in 2004.

6.text: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the human body.
Calcium is present in the maximum amount among elements in the human body.
Calcium phosphate is the maximum salt in human bones.
Protein is the most abundant organic constituent.
Root hairs absorb the maximum amount of water in plants.
Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air inhaled or exhaled forcibly.
Amla is the richest source of vitamin C.
Chilli is the richest source of vitamin C among vegetables.
Orange is another source of vitamin C.
Carrot is a source of vitamin A.
Mango is the richest source of vitamin A among the given fruits.
Wheat germ oil is a source of vitamin E.
Soybean has the highest protein content.
Soybean is the highest-protein grain.
Groundnut is the richest protein source among the given options.
Rice has the highest percentage of carbohydrate.
Fats provide the highest calories per unit.
Fats provide the maximum energy per gram.
Carbohydrate, fat, and protein together form the maximum energy-yielding diet group.
The biotransformation of ATP to ADP provides maximum energy.
RBCs are the most numerous blood cells.
WBCs are the largest blood cells.
WBCs are the fewest among the blood cells.
Neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes.
Basophils are the least common granulocytes.
Basophils are the least common WBCs by percentage.
Linseed oil has the maximum amount of α-linolenic acid among oilseeds.
Flaxseed is the richest source of α-linolenic acid.
Red light produces the maximum photosynthetic rate.
Red light at approximately 655 nm is the most effective wavelength for photosynthesis.
Chlorella has the maximum efficiency of converting solar energy into chemical energy.
The leaf has the maximum oil percentage in peppermint.
Seaweed is the richest natural source of iodine.
Lemon has the highest concentration of citrate among citrus fruits.
Mango is the richest source of vitamins A, B, and C.
Green vegetables are the richest source of iron.
Holstein–Friesian is the world's highest-production dairy animal breed.
Holstein–Friesian is a high milk-yielding cow breed.
Egg has the highest biological value among proteins.
Egg is a protein source containing all essential amino acids.
A protein has high biological value when its essential amino acids are present in appropriate proportion.
Vital capacity is approximately 3.5–4.5 L.
Vital capacity is higher in athletes and mountain dwellers.
Vital capacity is lower in women, elderly people, and smokers.
Red light produces the maximum rate of photosynthesis.
Red light is the most effective light for photosynthesis.
Blue light is the second most effective light for photosynthesis.
